sources.title: The Four Big Risks
sources.author: Marty Cagan / Silicon Valley Product Group
sources.principle: Distinguishes value, usability, feasibility, and business viability risks.
sources.limitation: A practitioner framework; not causal proof that a specific discovery process produces success.

sources.title: Using in-depth interviews
sources.author: GOV.UK Service Manual / User research community
sources.principle: Use a discussion guide, neutral questions, concrete examples, and clarification.
sources.limitation: Qualitative interview guidance; an interview account is not independent behavioral observation.

sources.title: Contextual research and observation
sources.author: GOV.UK Service Manual / User research community
sources.principle: Observe tasks in context, including real tools, documents, and barriers.
sources.limitation: Observed situations may not represent all users or cases.

sources.title: Applied cognitive task analysis (ACTA): a practitioner's toolkit for understanding cognitive task demands
sources.author: Laura G. Militello and Robert J. B. Hutton
sources.principle: A task diagram, knowledge audit, and simulation interview help expose cognitive demands for design.
sources.limitation: 1998 study in particular settings; Boring PM's adapted questions and agent implementation have not been validated by this study.
sources.pages_inspected: Scanned paper introduction and method sections; PDF pages 3–4 (1-based), plus PubMed abstract.

sources.title: Customer Interviews: How to Recruit, What to Ask, and How to Synthesize What You Learn
sources.author: Teresa Torres / Product Talk
sources.principle: Select participants relevant to the product's user or customer roles and recover specific accounts.
sources.limitation: Recruitment and story-based interviewing practices do not establish prevalence or willingness to buy by themselves.

sources.title: Jobs to Be Done Theory
sources.author: Clayton Christensen Institute
sources.principle: Understand desired progress and the circumstances and functional, social, and emotional forces behind choices.
sources.limitation: A useful explanatory lens, not a complete requirements or market-validation process.

sources.title: Opportunity Solution Trees: Visualize Your Discovery to Stay Aligned and Drive Outcomes
sources.author: Teresa Torres / Product Talk
sources.principle: Connect an outcome with opportunities, alternative solutions, and tests.
sources.limitation: Do not invent opportunities to fill a tree. A provisional map is not validated demand.

sources.title: Discovering Solutions: Quickly Determine Which Ideas Will Work (And Which Won't)
sources.author: Teresa Torres / Product Talk
sources.principle: Interviewing uncovers opportunities; assumption testing evaluates proposed solutions.
sources.limitation: Method description includes course promotion; use the conceptual distinction without treating it as comparative experimental evidence.

sources.title: The New User Story Backlog is a Map
sources.author: Jeff Patton
sources.principle: Keep the user's overall activity visible while organizing smaller deliverable stories.
sources.limitation: A mapping technique does not determine the correct product scope automatically.

sources.title: Set Boundaries — Shape Up
sources.author: Ryan Singer / Basecamp
sources.principle: Set an appetite for the work and adjust scope to fit it.
sources.limitation: Basecamp's team sizes and cycle lengths are contextual; Boring PM does not mandate them.

sources.title: RICE: Simple prioritization for product managers
sources.author: Sean McBride / Intercom
sources.principle: Compare reach, impact, confidence, and effort with consistent units.
sources.limitation: Scores depend on input quality and do not override essential dependencies or uncertainty.

sources.title: Appendix C: How to Write a Good Requirement
sources.author: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook
sources.principle: Use clear, singular, verifiable statements and explicitly manage assumptions and unresolved values.
sources.limitation: Adapt the rigor to software scope; this repository does not claim NASA certification or standards compliance.

sources.title: 4.2 Technical Requirements Definition
sources.author: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook
sources.principle: Check stakeholder alignment, traceability, assumptions, technical feasibility, and verifiability.
sources.limitation: The source describes systems engineering; Boring PM's small-product artifact chain is an adaptation.

sources.title: Example Mapping
sources.author: Cucumber Open Source Project
sources.principle: Separate a story's rules, concrete examples, and unresolved questions.
sources.limitation: Examples clarify behavior but do not prove code exists or works.

sources.title: Gherkin Reference
sources.author: Cucumber Open Source Project
sources.principle: Scenarios describe context, an event, and observable expected results.
sources.limitation: Text scenarios need step definitions, assertions, and execution before they provide test evidence.

sources.title: Using moderated usability testing
sources.author: GOV.UK Service Manual / User research community
sources.principle: Observe actual or likely users attempting relevant tasks with prototypes or services.
sources.limitation: A small usability study identifies issues; it does not demonstrate broad demand or long-term impact.

sources.title: Measuring the success of your service
sources.author: GOV.UK Service Manual / Performance analysis community
sources.principle: Combine performance data and user research, including complete journey assessment.
sources.limitation: Metrics need a task-specific definition, comparable baseline, and interpretation.

sources.title: WCAG 2 Overview
sources.author: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative
sources.principle: Introduces the WCAG standards and resources for accessible web content.
sources.limitation: This overview is not a complete conformance audit; consult selected normative criteria during implementation.

sources.title: Boring UI README
sources.author: hachej/boring-ui
sources.principle: Describes the chat/workbench architecture, Pi resources, plugins, packages, and app-owned hosting.
sources.limitation: Snapshot-specific. A documented framework capability is not a tested Boring PM integration.

sources.title: Boring Ask User README
sources.author: hachej/boring-ui
sources.principle: Documents ask_user forms, answers, persistence, and host composition.
sources.limitation: Capabilities require correct host installation and context. Limits and delivery behavior must be rechecked in the target version.

sources.title: Boring UI Plugin CLI README
sources.author: hachej/boring-ui
sources.principle: Distinguishes package creation from local runtime scaffolding and lists plugin verification commands.
sources.limitation: Manifest verification is not runtime proof. Dependencies and host support remain required.

sources.title: Boring UI package-plugin template manifest
sources.author: hachej/boring-ui
sources.principle: Shows a real package manifest with Pi and Boring resources and built entrypoints.
sources.limitation: The monorepo template contains workspace dependencies; it is not a standalone production app.

sources.title: Canva Model Context Protocol
sources.author: Canva Developers
sources.principle: Offers design creation/editing, discovery, assets, exports, and collaboration through a remote MCP service.
sources.limitation: Custom integration access and authentication need verification. A connector in this chat does not automatically exist in Boring PM.

sources.title: MCP tools and rate limits
sources.author: Canva Developers
sources.principle: Tool availability and output behavior depend on plans, permissions, and content licensing.
sources.limitation: Check current tools rather than assuming the connected client's surface equals the full provider API.

sources.title: MCP
sources.author: Craft Help Center
sources.principle: Documents AI access to Craft content and space-specific MCP connections.
sources.limitation: Exact tool discovery and permitted document scope must be checked in the chosen connection.

sources.title: Craft API
sources.author: Craft Help Center
sources.principle: Supports document search and mutation, tasks, and collection management through configured connections.
sources.limitation: API support does not prove a given MCP client exposes every action or that an integration is already installed.

sources.title: Tools and prompts — Figma MCP server
sources.author: Figma Developer Docs
sources.principle: Documents design context, screenshots, component mapping, and native design operations.
sources.limitation: Capabilities differ by client and server; generated code still requires adaptation and verification.

sources.title: gh repo create
sources.author: GitHub CLI manual
sources.principle: Documents creating public repositories and pushing an existing local repository with --source and --push.
sources.limitation: Requires an authenticated CLI and appropriate account permissions; unavailable in the authoring workspace.

sources.title: Understanding users who do not use digital services
sources.author: GOV.UK Service Manual / User research community
sources.principle: Distinguishes digital skills, confidence, access, and support needs; cautions that users can misjudge their own ability.
sources.limitation: Government service guidance about assisted digital support; Boring PM does not adopt its scale or claim a validated automated skills assessment.

sources.title: Compare and Contrast Decisions
sources.author: Product Talk
sources.principle: Generate alternatives for one opportunity, identify their critical assumptions, and compare evidence from testing those assumptions.
sources.limitation: Practitioner guidance; the candidate count, fit criteria, and recommendation protocol in Boring PM are original design choices, not comparative efficacy results.

sources.title: User Interviews 101
sources.author: Maria Rosala and Kara Pernice / Nielsen Norman Group
sources.principle: Use flexible, concrete interview questions and distinguish reported attitudes or behavior from observation of actual task performance.
sources.limitation: UX practice guidance; an interview-based profile is provisional and does not establish that a proposed product will be usable.
